name: Nanotube-mesh self-healing bridge deck
subtitle: a bridge deck that finds and heals cracks

effects.effect: rolled-up carbon sheets are stronger than steel and conduct like metal

effect: rolled-up carbon sheets are stronger than steel and conduct like metal
how: Many of the world's bridges are decades old, and cracks let in water and salt that rust the steel inside long before an inspector notices. A mesh of carbon nanotubes runs through a plastic layer in the deck; a new crack breaks some paths and raises the electrical resistance there, revealing where it is, and a current through the same mesh then warms that spot until the plastic melts and flows shut.
obstacle: Heating a bridge deck takes a lot of power, and the mesh must survive decades of salt and traffic.
why: Nanotube crack sensing and heat healing exist separately in labs; never combined in a structure.
real: Patents describe CNT polymer-concrete overlays with self-sensing and crack-triggered Joule-heating self-healing structures, and lab CNT self-sensing/heating composites exist; never combined in a deck.
